findings.reason: a node running this control gets a red log quoting a different refusal, and will either weaken the assertion or rebuild §7's `--reopen` gate inside §31, which is another section's defect.
findings.text: §31's second negative control reads "restores the advice refusal, which makes the advice case fail with the `--reopen requires a completed run` text", but that text is raised only inside `if reopen:` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2345) and `--reopen` itself refuses without `--write-path` (:2323), while the case it controls issues a plain `crew resume --advice` with no `--reopen`; a plain resume of a live round is refused by a different door entirely (`live_attempt_refusal`, reckon/crew/resumption.py:330-355, whose message keeps the advice at `refused_advice_path`), so the red log cannot carry the named text and the section's own deliverable ("no channel that reaches a worker mid-turn") is contradicted by the refusal it borrows

findings.reason: the section's first done-when case is unsatisfiable on the surface it names, so the node must invent an argument or a second lookup the plan does not scope, and its write paths (`review.py`, `crew_run_commands.py`) may not include the reader it then needs.
findings.text: §32's first change requires `crew check --review` to refuse "a record whose `review_run_id` is not the writing run's own id, naming the expected id", but `crew check` accepts exactly one of `--run` or `--record` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1274) and `review_record_refusals(record)` is handed only the record (reckon/crew/review.py:932), so no invocation knows both the record and the writer's id; `--run <review-run>` cannot supply the record either, because `stored_record` selects it by the run's own `review_run_id` (reckon/crew/review_records.py:677-740), which is precisely the truncated value the fix exists to detect

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `claims.py:157-158` (the `widen_takes_effect` docstring on fixed mounts), `claims.py:113-116` (`ClaimAmendmentRefusedError` for a live worker), `crew_run_commands.py:2345` (`--reopen requires a completed run`), `review.py:932` (`review_record_refusals`) and `crew_run_commands.py:1229` (`crew_repair_review`) all resolve at the reviewed revision; the section hrefs there are fragment anchors on this page.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §31's second negative control names a refusal text that the command its case runs cannot produce.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every log and note lands under the run directory (plan.html:175, 179, 183), which is durable and outside any session scratchpad or node-local temp path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose reach the symbols or test filenames these sections add.
rubric_items.reasoning: two findings — §31's control text and §32's `crew check --review` surface, the latter being a mechanism that cannot reach the state its done-when asserts.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — each of the three sections names one deliverable: §30 one investigation, §31 one repair (the round takes new input), §32 one mistyped-id repair with its write-time refusal.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §30, §31 and §32 declare no `depends-on` entries in `plan-section-depends-on` (plan.html:29) and need none: §31's advice half does not consume §7's halted-run reopen, and §32's repair path consumes no other section's output.
